class.name: HEGoCopiaInput
class.brief_description: Sends a Copia store to an HDA input as one point cloud, so a generator can see what the store holds and send back clear points for the cells it replaces (docs/copia/houdini.md).
class.description:
HEGo finds this handler because it extends [HEGoInputHandler]; neither HEGo nor Copia names the other. Wire the [code]CopiaStore3D[/code] node into an input row.
Row settings (the input's settings dictionary): [codeblock]
copia_input: true marks the row as a Copia input (SETTINGS_MARKER) rect: [x0, z0, x1, z1] optional; only the cells that intersect it, and only instance points inside it (store-local metres on X and Z). Absent = every cell. sets: ["roots"] optional; only these sets get cell points. Empty = every set. exclude_sets: ["roots"] optional; these sets get no cell points. points_of_sets: ["roads"] optional; the instance points of these sets (within rect) are sent too. Empty = none. Not limited by sets and exclude_sets. [/codeblock]
The cloud has two kinds of points, told apart by [code]hegocopia_cell_point[/code]: [codeblock]
cell points (hegocopia_cell_point = 1), one per cell and set that holds points: P (cell centre, y 0), hegocopia_cell, hegocopia_set, hegocopia_count (int), hegocopia_cell_min, hegocopia_cell_max (vector3) instance points (hegocopia_cell_point = 0), when points_of_sets names sets: P, N, up, scale, hegocopia_object, hegocopia_set, hegocopia_keep, Cd, hegocopia_custom + hegocopia_custom_w when the points have them, and each pass-through column under its own name [/codeblock]
Every attribute has a value for every point; the other kind's rows hold zero or an empty string. The cloud does not name its store: the HDA names the store it writes to with a string parameter of its own, stamped onto its output as [code]hegocopia_store[/code] (docs/copia/houdini.md). HEGo inputs carry int, float, vector3 and string attributes only, so the orientation travels as N + up + scale. The points are in the store's local space and are sent as they are: the HDA's output is written back into the store without a transform, so keep the HEGo node and the store at the same transform.
Nothing is filtered or interpreted here: which cell points to turn into clear points is the generator's recipe. A generator that clears must be cooked against the store's current content, so a row with this marker makes its cook strict.

method.name: requires_strict_cook
method.description: A generator that clears cells must see the store as it is.

method.name: build_points
method.description:
The point cloud of [param store] for the row settings in [param settings] (see the class comment): [code]{P, attributes, cell_count, instance_count, error}[/code], where [code]P[/code] and [code]attributes[/code] are exactly what [method HEGoInputNode.set_geo] takes (cell points first, then instance points; an empty store gives no points and no attributes, as HEGo rejects zero-length attribute arrays) and [code]error[/code] is empty unless the store or the settings cannot be used.
Also read from [param settings]: [code]input_path[/code], the value of [code]_hego_node_path[/code] (default: [code]store_path[/code], else the store's path from its scene root).
No loop over points: the columns come from the store as arrays and are joined as arrays.

constants.constant: Marks stored input settings as belonging to a Copia input, so its options and strict cook rule stay in force while the store is missing.
What an unbounded read covers, in metres.
to_attributes names the sent columns by.
